SPECIFICATIONS AND COST ESTIMATES FOR NEW RADAR INSTRUMENTATION AND ASSOCIATED ACQUISITION SOFTWARE WILL ALSO BE NEEDED.

ULTRASOUND SIMULATION FOR NDE (NONDESTRUCTIVE EVALUATION) OF COMPOSITES.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS TASK IS TO DEMONSTRATE THE USE OF NONDESTRUCTIVE EVALUATION (NDE) SIMULATION TOOLS TO IMPROVE INSPECTION OF AERONAUTIC COMPOSITES. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO ADVANCE ULTRASOUND SIMULATION TOOLS AND APPLY THEM TO COMPLEX GEOMETRY COMPOSITE INSPECTION SCENARIOS TO YIELD GUIDANCE ON OPTIMAL INSPECTION METHODS. BACKGROUND OF THE WORK: THIS WORK ARISES UNDER NASA AERONAUTICS RESEARCH MISSION DIRECTORATE (ARMD) ADVANCED COMPOSITES PROJECT (ACP). OVER THE PAST YEAR, NASA LANGLEY RESEARCH CENTER (LARC) HAS BEEN DEVELOPING A CUSTOM ULTRASOUND SIMULATION TOOL THAT IS BASED ON FINITE DIFFERENCE METHOD. THE CUSTOM TOOL SIMULATED 3D ULTRASONIC WAVE PROPAGATION IN COMPOSITE MATERIALS. CURRENTLY THE SIMULATION CODE HAS BEEN VALIDATED FOR FLAT COMPOSITES OF VARIOUS ANISOTROPIC PROPERTIES. INSPECTION CHALLENGE CASES OF COMPLEX GEOMETRY COMPOSITES HAVE BEEN PROVIDED TO NASA BY INDUSTRY WITH THE INTENT THAT THE CUSTOM LARC SIMULATION CODE WILL BE IMPLEMENTED TO REPRESENT INSPECTION OF THE INSPECTION CHALLENGE CASES. THE GOALS FOR THIS SOW ARE: VERIFY CODE FUNCTIONALITY FOR COMPLEX GEOMETRY COMPOSITES SIMULATE INSPECTION CHALLENGE CASES  YIELD SIMULATION-BASED GUIDANCE FOR OPTIMIZED NDE INSPECTION METHODS DEMONSTRATE THE USE OF NDE SIMULATION FOR INSPECTION OPTIMIZATION

BLOWN AIRFOIL CFD. THIS TASK WILL PERFORM COMPUTATIONAL FLUIDIC DYNAMIC (CFD) ANALYSIS ON A BLOWN WING CONFIGURATION TO DETERMINE AERO-PROPULSIVE PERFORMANCE. DISTRIBUTED ELECTRIC PROPULSION (DEP) ENABLES A HIGH DEGREE OF COUPLING BETWEEN THE AERODYNAMICS AND PROPULSION CHARACTERISTICS OF AIRCRAFT WING SYSTEMS. TIGHT COUPLING OF THESE TWO DISCIPLINES OFFER OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE THE PERFORMANCE AND ACHIEVE CAPABILITIES THAT CAN T BE ACHIEVED WITH ISOLATED WING AND PROPULSION SOLUTIONS. HIGHER-ORDER ANALYSIS USING CFD TOOLS IS REQUIRED TO CAPTURE THESE HIGHLY COUPLED EFFECTS WITH ANALYSIS TOOLS THAT HAVE BEEN CALIBRATED TO VALIDATION DATASETS FROM PRIOR AERO-PROPULSIVE WIND TUNNEL TESTS. ANALYSIS OF SPECIFIC DEP WING SYSTEMS IS DESIRED TO IMPROVE THE STATE OF THE ART TO ACHIEVE VERY HIGH LIFT AT LOW SPEEDS, AT EVEN STATIC CONDITIONS WHILE ENTRAINING FLOW TO MAXIMIZE THE WING LIFTING CHARACTERISTICS. AT THE SAME TIME HIGH CRUISE EFFICIENCY IS DESIRED, ALONG WITH EXCELLENT CONTROL CHARACTERISTICS THROUGHOUT THE FLIGHT ENVELOPE. THIS RESEARCH WILL INVESTIGATE SPECIFIC DEP CONFIGURATION TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE AERO-PROPULSIVE CHARACTERISTICS. EXISTING ANALYSIS WAS PERFORMED ON A GEOMETRY. THIS CURRENT STATEMENT OF WORK EXTENDS PREVIOUS WORK WITH MODIFICATIONS TO THE LOCATIONS AND SHAPE OF THE PROPULSORS, SLOT LOCATIONS, AND WING.

DEVELOPMENT OF A MULTIPLE SAMPLING EXTENSION FOR A MIXED INTEGER EFFICIENT GLOBAL OPTIMIZATION (AMIEGO) MIXED INTEGER NONLINEAR PROGRAMMING ALGORITHM.  A RECENTLY PUBLISHED ALGORITHM FOR MIXED INTEGER NONLINEAR PROGRAMMING, A MIXED INTEGER EFFICIENT GLOBAL OPTIMIZATION (AMIEGO), HAS SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCED THE STATE OF THE ART FOR SOLVING OPTIMIZATION PROBLEMS WITH BOTH INTEGER AND CONTINUOUS DESIGN VARIABLES. THIS ALGORITHM CAN BENEFIT GREATLY FROM EXPLOITING GRADIENT BASED OPTIMIZATION WITH ANALYTIC DERIVATIVES FOR ITS INNER OPTIMIZATION ROUTINE. NASA S OPENMDAO FRAMEWORK SPECIALIZES IN GRADIENT BASED OPTIMIZATION WITH ANALYTIC DERIVATIVES, WHICH MAKES IT A NATURAL PLACE TO IMPLEMENT THE NEWLY CREATED AMIEGO ALGORITHM. THERE ARE A NUMBER OF INTERESTING MIXED INTEGER NONLINEAR PROGRAMMING PROBLEMS THAT ARE OF INTEREST TO NASA AERONAUTICS RESEARCH MISSION DIRECTORATE S (ARMD) TRANSFORMATIONAL TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES (TTT) PROJECT, INCLUDING THE SOLUTION TO A LARGE SCALE WING TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION OPTIMIZATION PROBLEM. THE GOAL OF THIS WORK IS TO IMPLEMENT THE AMIEGO ALGORITHM WITHIN OPENMDAO, USING A MULTIPLE SAMPLING BASED INFILL CRITERION AND THEN TO DEMONSTRATE THE ALGORITHM ON THE SOLUTION OF THE WING OPTIMIZATION PROBLEM.

WIND-TUNNEL BALANCE DESIGN TRADE STUDY.  WIND-TUNNEL BALANCES ARE THE PRIMARY SOURCE FOR AERODYNAMIC FORCE AND MOMENT DATA IN GROUND-BASED AERONAUTICS RESEARCH. BUT, BALANCES ARE TIME CONSUMING AND COSTLY TO MANUFACTURE. THE TIME AND COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH BALANCE FABRICATION ARE PRIMARILY DRIVEN BY THE BLIND CUTS THAT ARE OFTEN SPECIFIED DURING THE DESIGN PROCESS. THESE CUTS ALMOST ALWAYS REQUIRE BALANCE MANUFACTURERS TO RESORT TO USING ELECTRICAL DISCHARGE MACHINING (EDM) WITH COMPLEX FLAG SHAPED ELECTRODES TO ACHIEVE THE BLIND CUTS.   THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS WORK IS TO RESEARCH WIND-TUNNEL BALANCE DESIGNS THAT DO NOT REQUIRE BLIND CUTS TO ACHIEVE THE MEASUREMENT GOALS AND ULTIMATELY PERMIT BALANCE FABRICATION TO BE COMPLETED USING HIGHER SPEED MILLING, DRILLING, AND GRINDING OPERATIONS.  ELIMINATING BLIND CUTS FROM THE DESIGN MAY NECESSITATE REDUCING THE MOMENT OF INERTIA OF THE BALANCE AT SECTIONS ALONG THE BALANCE LENGTH. THE REDUCED MOMENT OF INERTIA WILL LIKELY RESULT IN INCREASED BALANCE DEFLECTION AND STRESSES ALONG WITH A DECREASED RESONANT FREQUENCY. THUS, ANOTHER OBJECTIVE OF THIS WORK WILL BE TO QUANTITATIVELY ESTIMATE THE EFFECT OF THE NEW DESIGNS ON THE DEFLECTION, STRESS, AND RESONANT FREQUENCY.

IGF::OT::IGF     TASK ORDER - STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW)  TASK TITLE:  FLIGHTDECK INTERVAL MANAGEMENT (FIM) DISPLAY ELEMENTS, INFORMATION,&ANNUNCIATIONS DATABASE EXTENSION  1.0 INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND:  FLIGHTDECK INTERVAL MANAGEMENT (FIM) OPERATIONS, AS DESCRIBED IN THE FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATIONS (FAA) NEXT GENERATION AIR TRANSPORTATION SYSTEM (NEXTGEN), AIM TO INCREASE EFFICIENCY OF OPERATIONS BY IMPROVING THE CONSISTENCY OF INTER-ARRIVAL RATES.  IN THE PROPOSED FIM CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS, AN AIRCRAFT THAT IS EQUIPPED WITH ADS-B MAY BE CLEARED BY A CONTROLLER TO ACHIEVE AND/OR MAINTAIN AN INTERVAL RELATIVE TO ANOTHER AIRCRAFT.  PILOTS ARE PROVIDED WITH A SPEED TARGET AND A LOCATION AT WHICH TO ACHIEVE THIS SPEED (THE ACHIEVE-BY POINT), AND A TRAFFIC-TO-FOLLOW (TTF) AIRCRAFT IDENTIFIER IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE THIS INTERVAL.  FIM OPERATIONS ARE PURPORTED TO INCREASE THROUGHPUT, REDUCE TACTICAL MANEUVERING (ESPECIALLY VECTORING), REDUCE CONTROLLER WORKLOAD, AND REDUCE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT BY ENABLING OPTIMIZED PROFILE DESCENTS (AKA CONTINUOUS DESCENT ARRIVALS).  FUTURE CONCEPTS OF OPERATIONS ENVISION REDUCED INTERACTION WITH CONTROLLERS AND INCREASED AUTOMATION.  THE QUESTION AT HAND IS HOW TECHNOLOGY, PROCEDURES, AND PILOT TRAINING SHOULD BE DESIGNED TO EFFECTIVELY SUPPORT FIM OPERATIONS.    IN RECENT YEARS, FIM RESEARCH HAS BEEN CONDUCTED AT NASA LANGLEY UNDER THE AIRSPACE SYSTEMS PROGRAM AND AT A SMALL NUMBER OF OTHER LABORATORIES AND INSTITUTIONS.  UNDER THE PRIOR NASA FLIGHT CRITICAL SYSTEMS RESEARCH (FCSR) CONTRACT / TASK ORDER (I.E., NNL06AA05B, TASK ORDER NNL13AB30T), NASA AND THE FAA SPONSORED THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CITATION DATABASE AND ASSOCIATED MULTIMEDIA RELATIONAL DATABASE OF FIM LITERATURE AND FLIGHT DECK INTERFACE DESIGN CONCEPTS.  THE OBJECTIVE OF THAT PRIOR AWARD WAS TO PROVIDE TOOLS TO THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY SUCH THAT FUTURE RESEARCH COULD BENEFIT FROM A COMMON AND ACCESSIBLE REPOSITORY OF PRIOR EFFORTS, TO FACILITATE COMPARISON AND SUMMARIZATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, AND TO ENCOURAGE THE FUTURE INCORPORATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS AND DESIGN CONCEPTS IN THIS REPOSITORY.   AS PART OF THE PREVIOUS TASK ORDER NNL13AB30T, NASA AND THE FAA IDENTIFIED ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONALITY THAT WOULD BE BENEFICIAL TO THE RESEARCH COMMUNITY.  THIS NEW EFFORT WILL AUGMENT THE PRIOR DEVELOPMENT OF THE LITERATURE DATABASE AND THE FIM CONCEPTS DATABASE.   2.0  SCOPE&OBJECTIVE(S):  2.1 THE SCOPE OF THIS EFFORT IS TO AUGMENT THE LITERATURE DATABASE AND THE FIM CONCEPTS DATABASE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED UNDER TASK ORDER NNL13AB30T, AS DEFINED BY THE SPECIFIC TASKS BELOW.    2.2 THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS TASK ORDER IS TO DELIVER UPDATED DATABASES AND ASSOCIATED USER INTERFACE MECHANISMS, EXTEND THE CONCEPTS AND TOOLS, PROVIDE PRESENTATION MATERIAL, AND DEVELOP A SOFTWARE MIGRATION PLAN FOR THE AFOREMENTIONED FIM LITERATURE AND CONCEPTS DATABASE.  3.0 DESCRIPTION OF THE WORK/TASKS TO BE PERFORMED:    THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING TASKS:     3.1 UPDATE DATABASE CONTENT&ENSURE VERSION INFORMATION AVAILABLE   3.1.1  AT A MINIMUM, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CONDUCT ONLINE DATABASE SEARCHES AND CONTACT RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS/PERSONS (WITH CC TO TECH POC) CURRENTLY INCLUDED IN THE DATABASES TO OBTAIN PUBLICATIONS AND RESEARCH NOTES COMPLETED SINCE THE PRIOR LITERATURE REVIEW CONDUCTED UNDER TASK ORDER NNL13AB30T. THE PROPOSED EXTENSION OF THE SBIR PHASE II IS AIMED AT EXTENDING THE TECHNIQUES, METHODOLOGY AND TOOLS OF THE AUTONOMOUS, CLOSED-LOOP PROCEDURAL GUIDANCE SYSTEM, DESIGNATED AS VULCAN (VISUAL ULTRASOUND LEARNING CONTROL AND ANALYSIS NETWORK), DEVELOPED FOR THE FLEXIBLE ULTRASOUND SYSTEM DEVELOPED (FUS) BY GE FOR NASA S EXPLORATION MEDICAL CAPABILITY GROUP. THE WORK DONE DURING PHASE I AND II OF THIS SBIR FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING THE CORE TECHNOLOGY TO ENABLE 3- DIMENSIONAL PROCEDURAL GUIDANCE AND ULTRASOUND DEVICE CONTROL THROUGH A MICROSOFT HOLOLENS AUGMENTED REALITY (AR) INTERFACE. THE SYSTEM HAS BEEN EXTENDED TO ENABLE SOME PLUG-N-PLAY CAPABILITIES THROUGH DYNAMIC CONNECTIVITY TO A STANDARDIZED ELECTRONIC PROCEDURE LIBRARY (EPROC OR PROX) AT NASA. A DEEP MACHINE LEARNING (DML) APPLICATION MONITORS PROCEDURAL EXECUTION, PROVIDING CLOSED-LOOP PERFORMANCE FEEDBACK AND DRIVING USERS TOWARDS CORRECT PROCEDURAL EXECUTION AND OUTCOMES. FINALLY, WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED REMOTE, SECURE CONNECTIVITY TO AMES S  MEDICS  DML-BASED DECISION SUPPORT TOOL THAT CAN RECEIVE AND INTERPRET ULTRASOUND IMAGES GENERATED BY VULCAN AND THEN SEND BACK DECISION SUPPORT RESULTS FOR DISPLAY TO THE USER IN THE HOLOLENS. THUS, THE CURRENT SOLUTION IS A DIGITAL PLATFORM SEAMLESSLY INTEGRATING THE FOLLOWING COMPONENTS:  AUGMENTED REALITY ENABLED ELECTRONIC MEDICAL PROCEDURE TOOLSET, AUGMENTED REALITY HEADSET, ADAPTIVE USER INTERFAC, DEEP MACHINE LEARNING TOOLSET FOR IMAGE ANALYSIS, NAVIGATIONAL GUIDANCE SYSTEM, LIBRARY OF MEDICAL PROCEDURE WITH CORRESPONDING TRAINING MATERIAL, AND PATIENT SPECIFIC MEDICAL AND ANATOMICAL INFORMATION

IGF::OT::IGFIN THE CURRENT PHASE II PROJECT, ULTRAMET IS DEVELOPING A FULLY FUNCTIONAL THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) LASER-DIRECTED CHEMICAL VAPOR DEPOSITION (LCVD) SYSTEM WITH THE APPROPRIATE CONTROLS TO ENSURE LAYER-TOLAYER CONSISTENCY AND FINE RESOLUTION IN A 6" CUBIC WRITING VOLUME. THE CURRENT SYSTEM IS DESIGNED TO PRINT OBJECTS IN DENSE RHENIUM OR TUNGSTEN DIRECTLY FROM A 3D DIGITAL GEOMETRY USING HEXAFLUORIDE (REF6 OR WF6) PRECURSOR GASES. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II-X ENHANCEMENT IS TO EXPAND THE 3D-LCVD CAPABILITY TO MOLYBDENUM WHILE ENABLING DEPOSITION FROM LOWER-COST CHLORIDE PRECURSORS. MOLYBDENUM PENTACHLORIDE (MOCL5) IS OVER AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE LESS EXPENSIVE THAN MOLYBDENUM HEXAFLUORIDE (MOF6), THE ANALOG TO THE RHENIUM AND TUNGSTEN HEXAFLUORIDES USED IN THE PHASE I AND PHASE II EFFORTS. FURTHER, CHLORIDES CAN BE PRODUCED IN SITU IN THE REACTOR BY FLOWING CHLORINE GAS THROUGH A HEATED BED OF METAL PELLETS, FURTHER REDUCING COST AND SIMPLIFYING PRECURSOR SUPPLY REQUIREMENTS. THIS OPTION IS NOT POSSIBLE WITH FLUORINE DUE TO ITS EXTREME REACTIVITY. THE USE OF MOCL5 WILL REQUIRE A HEATED CHAMBER TO EXCEED THE 268 C BOILING POINT TO ENABLE A FULL ATMOSPHERE OF PRESSURE WITHIN THE REACTOR. IN CONTRAST, MOST HEXAFLUORIDES ARE GASES AT OR JUST ABOVE ROOM TEMPERATURE. WHILE THIS HAS SIMPLIFIED SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT TO DATE, DEVELOPMENT OF A HEATED CHAMBER WILL SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE CONSUMABLE COSTS AND ELIMINATE CORROSION ATTRIBUTED TO THE CHEMICALLY AGGRESSIVE HYDROGEN FLUORIDE (HF) BYPRODUCT.

RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS OF IN SITU AND ON-ORBIT OBSERVATIONS OF THE ASIAN TROPOPAUSE AEROSOL LAYER (BATAL - ATAL). THE ASIAN TROPOPAUSE AEROSOL LAYER (ATAL) IS AN ENHANCEMENT OF AEROSOLS IN THE UPPER TROPOSPHERE AND LOWER STRATOSPHERE (UTLS) ASSOCIATED WITH DEEP CONVECTION OF BOUNDARY-LAYER POLLUTION DURING THE ASIAN SUMMER MONSOON. THE PRESENCE OF ATAL HAS IMPORTANT IMPLICATIONS FOR CLOUD FORMATION, PRECIPITATION, UTLS CHEMISTRY, AND REGIONAL CLIMATE. A BALLOON MEASUREMENT CAMPAIGN OF THE ATAL (BATAL) IS A UNIQUE AND EFFECTIVE WAY TO VALIDATE SATELLITE OBSERVATIONS AND OBTAIN MORE INFORMATION ON THE PHYSICAL AND CHEMICAL PROPERTIES OF THE ATAL THROUGH BALLOON-BORNE INSTRUMENTS. UNDER FUNDING FROM THE NASA HEADQUARTERS EARTH SCIENCE DIVISION UPPER ATMOSPHERE RESEARCH PROGRAM (UARP) AND ATMOSPHERIC COMPOSITION MODELING AND ANALYSIS PROGRAM (ACMAP) RESEARCH&ANALYSIS PROGRAMS THIS TASK BUILDS UPON PRIOR WORK TO THE ACQUIRE, PROCESS, ANALYZE, INTERPRET AND DISSEMINATE OBSERVATIONAL DATA FROM SATELLITES, BALLOONS AND AIRCRAFT TO ILLUMINATE THE OPTICAL PROPERTIES, COMPOSITION, AND POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF THE ATAL ON THE UTLS REGION.

THE SUCCESSFUL EXECUTION OF THE LARC (LANGLEY RESEARCH CENTER) ROLE ON CIRAS (COMMERCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE FOR ROBOTIC ASSEMBLY AND SERVICES) WILL REQUIRE DEVELOPMENT AND REFINEMENT OF TALISMAN (TENDON-ACTUATED LIGHTWEIGHT IN-SPACE MANIPULATOR) AND NINJAR (NASA INTELLIGENT JIGGING AND ASSEMBLY ROBOTS) CONTROL ALGORITHMS. NASA/LARC SEEKS SUPPORT IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND EXECUTION OF THESE ALGORITHMS AND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ALGORITHMS IN MATLAB, GAZEBO, ROS, AND SPEEDGOAT ENVIRONMENTS. THIS EFFORT WILL REQUIRE THE CONVERSION AND MODIFICATION OF EXISTING CONTROL ALGORITHMS PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED BY NASA AND RE-CONFIGURING THEM FOR USE IN NEW COMPUTING ENVIRONMENTS. THE TASK WILL ALSO REQUIRE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW CONTROL ALGORITHMS AND STRATEGIES FOR THE NEW TALISMAN AND NINJAR 2.0 AND 3.0 SYSTEMS PRESENTLY UNDER DEVELOPMENT UNDER THE CIRAS CONTRACT. THE RESULT OF ALL OF THIS WORK WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A CONTROL SYSTEM SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR THE TALISMAN 2.0/3.0 ARCHITECTURES TO BE DEMONSTRATED AT LARC IN FY18.
